subject: Soft commit proposal and seasonal floor for Q1 launch
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@launchgrid.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Ellis <morgan.ellis@launchgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying ramp credits & monthly soft commit for Jan launch

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We're locking in a Jan 2027 limited public launch and need to finalize how we handle usage economics for the first three months. Two quick asks: 

- Can you outline a "soft" monthly commit schedule (step-up) that lets us start small in Jan and scale aggressively in Feb/Mar while preserving predictable unit pricing?
- How do surge credits / seasonal floors work for a launch window? Our product has a burst profile in week 1 and again around a mid-launch campaign in week 4.

We're prepared to provide a short usage forecast (attached) and a list of endpoints. Procurement will want clear terms for true-ups and early termination. Can your commercial team propose a simple structure we can review with legal?

Appreciate it — cc'ing Morgan (ops) and procurement so we can keep everyone aligned.

Best,
Alex
VP Product, LaunchGrid Inc.

Attachments: LaunchGrid_usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@launchgrid.com>
Cc: Morgan Ellis <morgan.ellis@launchgrid.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying ramp credits & monthly soft commit for Jan launch

Hi Alex — great to hear about the Jan launch timeline. Based on the forecast you shared, here's a practical soft-commit structure that balances predictability for LaunchGrid and flexibility for the bursty launch weeks. I've attached a short term sheet with numbers and a clear True-Up flow.

High level proposal (month = calendar month):
- Month 1 (Jan): Soft commit = 150M input tokens/month baseline. Billing at committed rate up to baseline. Surge buffer: 50% over baseline (i.e., up to 225M) covered by 2 one-time launch credits (apply automatically for first two overages).
- Month 2 (Feb): Soft commit steps to 350M tokens/month. Committed discount applies above 150M up to 350M.
- Month 3 (Mar) and ongoing: Commit target 500M tokens/month (annualize after month 3 if you want to lock).

Discount bands (hosted per-token):
- 0–150M: list price (no discount)
- 150–350M: 8% committed discount
- 350–500M: 12% committed discount
- >500M: tiered volume pricing available; we can table a higher tier if your forecast moves there.

True-up and seasonality guardrails:
- Monthly true-up: any usage over the committed tier is billed at the committed-overage rate, with one-time launch credits applied for the two high-burst events in month 1.
- Seasonal floor: if month-on-month usage drops below 60% of committed tier for two consecutive months, we re-open a 30-day check-in to reset the tier or apply a prorated credit.
- Early termination: standard 60-day notice with prorated reconciliation on committed amounts.

Operational notes:
- We can add automatic fallbacks to a lower-latency cheaper model if you prefer tight cost controls during campaigns.
- We'll include per-endpoint token caps and alerting in Console so your ops team won't be surprised.

I've cc'd Rachel from Commercial — she'll follow up with an updated PDF term sheet and a DocuSign link if you want to proceed. If this structure looks acceptable, please confirm and we will convert to a draft SOW.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_soft_commit_term_sheet.pdf (term sheet with pricing bands and surge credit rules)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: LaunchGrid negotiation play — recommended concessions

Team — internal note before we send the formal SOW. Alex asked for soft commit + surge protection. Key negotiation levers and my recommendation: 

1) Concession we can make today: 12% discount band at 350–500M (lock for 3 months) instead of standard 10% for that band. Rationale: short-term incentive to hit the higher tier; low risk if they true-up.

2) Surge credits: offer 2 one-time launch credits that automatically apply to month 1 overages (up to 50% over baseline). After that, charge overage at committed-overage rate — keeps exposure contained.

3) Seasonal floor flexibility: include a clause that allows 1x 30-day reset within the first 90 days if campaign performance drops. This avoids immediate churn while preserving our economics.

4) Approval thresholds: any permanent reduction of committed tier or extra credits beyond the initial 2 requires manager approval (Ben). If they want >500M guaranteed capacity, route to infra for Dedicated pricing.

Next steps: Rachel — please prepare a DocuSign draft with the numbers above and include the HubSpot deal id LG-2026-087. Ben — please pre-approve the 12% concession so I can present it as firm.

Thanks,
Irene

1) Can you add a short SLA ramp clause that guarantees support response times for the first 30 days of launch (P1 within 1 hour)? We want that baked into the SOW in case of high-impact issues.
2) Please confirm the DocuSign link and who will be the signing contact on Redwood's side. Procurement needs a named signee.

If you can add the SLA clause and share the DocuSign draft, we can route internally and aim to sign by next Tue.

Appreciate the fast turn-around.

Best,
Alex
